Study exercise derived from this source. Explain the approach in your own words, work through an example, and identify edge cases. For code, implement your own version and discuss its time and space complexity.

import java.util.*;
class Main {
    public static int countMappings(String s)
    {
        int n = s.length();
        int count = 0;
        
        for(int i=0;i<n;i++)
        {
            if (s.charAt(i) != '0') {
                count++;
            }
        }
        
        for(int i=0;i<n;i++)
        {
            if (i + 1 < n)
            {
                int num = Integer.parseInt(s.substring(i, i+2));
                if (num >= 10 && num <= 26) {
                    count++;
                }
            }
        }
        return count;
    }
    public static void main(String[] args) {
       String s = "000";
       System.out.println(countMappings(s));
    }
}
